# Opcode `0x80` Minority Consumer-Path Audit

## Goal

Close the `Pass 6` scene-local follow-up left after `Opcode80SharedStub` was
confirmed:

do the minority `0x80` scenes still point to a hidden direct consumer, or do
they collapse cleanly into neighboring SFX, queue, music, or same-title
variant behavior?

This pass focuses only on the targeted minority cases named by the campaign
handoff:

- later-rearm scenes `MAP290` and `MAP334`
- the queue-plus-music scene `MAP415`
- the same-title contrast `MAP026` versus `MAP408`

## Method

- Parse the checked-in decoded scripts for those `5` scenes.
- For every `0x80` burst, record the neighboring sound-family opcodes that
  appear since the previous `0x80` and before the next one.
- Preserve the structured result as
  [`opcode_0x80_consumer_path_scan.json`](opcode_0x80_consumer_path_scan.json),
  generated by
  [`../verification/analyze_opcode_0x80_consumer_paths.py`](../verification/analyze_opcode_0x80_consumer_paths.py).

## Corpus result

The minority set now splits cleanly into already-known neighboring paths:

- `2 / 5` scenes are dominant-template openers that only stage explicit sound
  neighbors later in-file: `MAP290` and `MAP334`
- `1 / 5` scene is a queue-plus-music case with no in-file SFX pair:
  `MAP415`
- the last `2 / 5` scenes are the same-title Gallows contrast:
  `MAP026` is audio-heavy before its first `0x80`, while `MAP408` keeps only
  the inert paired `0x41/0x42` scaffold
- `3 / 5` of these scenes still reach the first `0x80` with no neighboring
  sound-family opcode at all, but `3 / 5` also stage explicit neighboring
  pairs later in the file

That is not the shape of a hidden direct `0x80` consumer.
It is the shape of scene-local branching between structural opener reuse and
already-known neighboring sound preparation.

## `MAP290` and `MAP334`: template openers, later neighboring consumers

[`MAP290`](../../decoded_scripts/14-Abandoned%20Mines%20B2/290-Dining%20in%20Darkness.txt)
and
[`MAP334`](../../decoded_scripts/18-Limestone%20Quarry/334-Torture%20Without%20End.txt)
both begin the same way:

- the first burst is the dominant paired scaffold
  `80 01 41 80 7F` then `80 01 42 80 7F`
- neither file has any sound-family opcode before that opener

What changes is what happens later.
Both files stage explicit neighboring sound-family work after the structural
opener instead of asking `0x80` itself to become the sound action:

- `MAP290` follows the second opener burst with the `0x85/0x88` SFX path, then
  later wraps `0x80` bursts with `0x9D`, `0x90`, `0x9E`, `0x99`, and a later
  `0x92` music-play beat
- `MAP334` is even tighter:
  immediately after the second opener burst it stages `0x85`, `0x86`, `0x88`,
  `0x9D`, `0x9E`, `0x90`, and `0x99` before the later `0x80` sequence starts

So these scenes do not rescue a direct-sound meaning for `0x80`.
They show a dominant structural opener followed by explicit neighboring
consumer setup.

## `MAP415`: queue-plus-music without an SFX pair

[`MAP415`](../../decoded_scripts/23-Great%20Cathedral/415-The%20Dark%20tempts%20Ashley.txt)
remains the strongest minority non-SFX example, and it still stays on the
neighboring-consumer side:

- before the first `0x80`, the file stages
  `0x9D`, `0x9E`, `0x90`, `0x99`, and `0x92`
- there is no `0x85/0x88` SFX pair anywhere in the file
- later in the same scene, the file refreshes the music-slot side again with
  `0x90 B0 02` and `0x99 02` before the later `0x0533` burst

That keeps `MAP415` inside the already-known queue-plus-music explanation.
It is still a minority neighboring-path case, not evidence that `0x80` itself
became the consumer.

## `MAP026` versus `MAP408`: same-title variant split

The Gallows pair now gives the cleanest same-title contrast:

- [`MAP026`](../../decoded_scripts/1-Wine%20Cellar/026-The%20Gallows.txt)
  stages all three prepared-state families before the first `0x80`:
  `0x9D/0x9E`, `0x90/0x92`, and `0x85/0x88`
- [`MAP408`](../../decoded_scripts/1-Wine%20Cellar/408-The%20Gallows%20(Mino%20Zombie,%20new%20chest).txt)
  stages none of them anywhere in the file and keeps only the inert paired
  `0x41/0x42` scaffold

That split is hard to read as a second `0x80` consumer.
It looks much more like scene-state or authoring variation inside the same
room family.

## Safe takeaway

- the minority scene-local follow-ups no longer argue for a hidden direct
  consumer behind `0x80`
- `MAP290` and `MAP334` still reduce to structural openers plus later explicit
  neighboring setup
- `MAP415` stays a queue-plus-music case without needing an SFX-based rescue
- `MAP026` versus `MAP408` is best read as same-title variant divergence, not
  handler-level contradiction

What remains open is therefore optional cleanup, not a blocker:
if future work wants to explain *which* downstream subsystem consumes each
prepared-state path in these scenes, that is a neighboring-opcode question,
not a reason to reopen `0x80` itself.
